name: Lixir Finance
rootCause: Broken Signature Verification. Lost: 2.60 ETH, 4,477.72 USDC, 3,609.95 USDT, 24,182.56 LIX

descriptions.text: Broken Signature Verification. Lost: 2.60 ETH, 4,477.72 USDC, 3,609.95 USDT, 24,182.56 LIX

Lixir Finance's vault tokens (lv_* wrappers over Uniswap V3 LP positions) were exploited due to a broken EIP-2612 permit signature verification. The attacker reused a single dummy signature to bypass checks, granting approval to their contract over dozens of holders' tokens, then drained underlying assets (WETH, USDC, USDT, LIX) via withdrawFrom/withdrawETHFrom, resulting in ~$12,300 loss.

On 25 June 2026, Lixir Finance's Ethereum vault system was exploited via a forged permit signature vulnerability. The attacker reused a single EIP-2612 signature to gain fraudulent approvals, draining over $12,300 in USDC, USDT, ETH, and LIX from multiple vault-share contracts. Lixir's custom permit implementation failed to check that the recovered signer matched the provided owner. This enabled arbitrary approvals via forged signatures, allowing unauthorized withdrawal of vault-share assets.
